diagnostic_evidence.quote: (or analytic contraction semigroups if the coefficients $\alpha_{j}$'s and $\beta_{j}$'s are complex)

issues.failure_explanation: All schemes of order >= 3 used (prop333, splitU, thm:added-1, thm:added-2) have complex coefficients, and Theorem ha requires analytic semigroups in that case. Koopman semigroups T(t)g=g(sigma(t,x)) on C_b(Omega) of a real flow are only defined for real t>=0 and are not analytic; e^{alpha t K_i} for complex alpha is undefined in the paper's framework (the frozen states become complex and leave Omega). Hence the remark's extension claim is unsupported, and the order claims C t^4/n^3 in Remark remApp(c) and the higher-order 3D algorithm (app33) have no justification within the paper's theory. Even for real coefficients, the hypotheses of Theorem ha (subspace U with E_{p+1}e^{tK}u uniformly bounded) are never verified for the Koopman operators on unbounded Omega with unbounded F.

failure_location.quote: Since the proof of Theorem \ref{ha} given  in \cite{JD5} is of an algebraic nature, it can be extended to bi-continuous contraction semigroups without changing any of arguments.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict to real-analytic (e.g. polynomial) F, interpret complex-time frozen flows via analytic continuation, and invoke classical ODE composition-method order theory for complex-coefficient splittings instead of the bi-continuous semigroup argument; drop the remark's unqualified extension claim.
issues.overall_effect: The theoretical error-bound guarantees for the complex higher-order splitting algorithms applied to nonlinear ODEs (Sections 4.2, 4.4, Appendix app33) are not established; only the numerical evidence remains.
issues.title: Complex-coefficient higher-order schemes are outside the bi-continuous Koopman framework; claimed extension of Hansen–Ostermann and pointwise orders unsupported
issues.why_classification: A replacement argument with an added analyticity hypothesis is needed, but the schemes and their advertised orders survive under that restriction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $D(\K)$ and $(\lambda_0 I - \K)D(\K)$ are bi-dense in $X$ for some $\lambda_0 > \omega\ge 0$

issues.failure_explanation: The remark deduces g(sigma(t,x))=lim (V(t/n))^n g(x) ('Thus') from the mere assumption that the full ODE has unique global solutions. Two gaps: (i) the frozen one-dimensional problems x'=F_1(x,x_2) need not have global solutions staying in Omega (e.g. x'=x^2 y, y'=-x^2 y is globally solvable since x+y is conserved, but the frozen problem x'=y x^2 with y>0 blows up in finite time), so e^{tK_1} on C_b(Omega) is not defined for all t; (ii) Chernoff's Theorem CPFBi requires a core D with V'(0+)g=Kg as a norm limit and (lambda_0-K)D bi-dense, plus uniform local bi-equicontinuity of V(t)^m; none is checked, and for unbounded F on unbounded Omega the sup-norm difference quotient of V(t)g need not converge for smooth g. The same unverified chain appears in Remark rem324 and Section 4's claim that K_i 'generates the semigroup' e^{tK_i}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add hypotheses (global solvability and Omega-invariance of the frozen problems, F locally Lipschitz/C^1) and either verify the Chernoff hypotheses on a suitable core or replace the semigroup argument by the classical ODE convergence proof for splitting methods.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence guarantee sigma(t,x)=lim x_n(t,x) for the Lie–Trotter/Strang algorithms (and the stated orders C t^2/n, C t^3/n^2) is unsupported as a consequence of the paper's theory; the methods are only justified empirically.
issues.title: Splitting algorithms asserted to converge via Chernoff's formula without verifying its hypotheses or well-definedness of frozen sub-flows
issues.why_classification: A contained but nontrivial argument and extra hypotheses are required; the algorithms and their conclusions survive under those hypotheses.
